claims.text: hnswlib describes M as the number of bi-directional links created for every new element during construction, with a reasonable range of 2-100. Atlas describes maxEdges as the maximum number of edges per node, with a range of 16-64 and a default of 16, meaning outgoing edges at each layer. Because ranges and degree semantics differ between implementations, check each implementation's own documentation. Sources: https://github.com/nmslib/hnswlib/blob/master/ALGO_PARAMS.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md

The 2026-10-23 MongoDB documentation snapshot gives numEdgeCandidates an inclusive range of 100–3200 and a default of 100. It limits the candidate nodes evaluated when finding neighbors for a newly inserted node. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Increasing graph connectivity can improve recall, but stores more links and increases indexing work. MongoDB warns that maxEdges can also slow queries because each visited node has more neighbors to evaluate. (high confidence)

In the MongoDB query-documentation snapshot dated 2026-10-14, ANN numCandidates must be at least limit and at most 10000. MongoDB recommends starting with at least 20 times limit, then tuning for the dataset and query requirements. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A larger construction candidate list can improve graph quality, which can raise recall, but at a cost to indexing and query speed. For hnswlib's ef_construction, improvements eventually stop. Atlas numEdgeCandidates is the index-time analogue of query-time numCandidates (the maximum number of nodes evaluated to find neighbors to connect to a new node), not the requested result count. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md ; https://github.com/nmslib/hnswlib/blob/master/ALGO_PARAMS.md

Increasing ef_construction has diminishing returns: hnswlib explicitly warns that index quality eventually stops improving. Pinecone's Faiss parameter sweep on Sift1M varied M, efSearch and efConstruction together and showed that recall and search time depend on all three, rather than on one universally optimal setting. Sources: https://github.com/nmslib/hnswlib/blob/master/ALGO_PARAMS.md ; https://www.pinecone.io/learn/series/faiss/hnsw/

HNSW separates graph connectivity, construction search effort, and query search breadth. Atlas exposes construction controls as hnswOptions.maxEdges and hnswOptions.numEdgeCandidates; query-time numCandidates is a separate setting. (high confidence)

In the MongoDB index documentation snapshot dated 2026-10-23, indexingMethod defaults to hnsw and hnswOptions applies only to hnsw indexes. MongoDB recommends retaining construction defaults unless large indexes have suboptimal recall. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

The 2026-10-23 MongoDB documentation snapshot gives maxEdges an inclusive range of 16–64 and a default of 16. It controls the maximum graph connections per node; these bounds are Atlas product settings, not universal HNSW limits. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Increasing the query-time search breadth (numCandidates) generally improves recall at the cost of query latency. It is a separate parameter from the construction-time setting numEdgeCandidates, which has its own recall and latency effects. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md

Do not assume that construction effort has zero effect on query latency. MongoDB explicitly warns that increasing numEdgeCandidates can affect latency, and Pinecone's Faiss experiment observed search-time differences across efConstruction values. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md ; https://www.pinecone.io/learn/series/faiss/hnsw/

Elliott and Clark's 2024 study reports that insertion order based on local intrinsic dimensionality or categories can shift HNSW recall by up to 12 percentage points in its experiments. This scopes parameter-only explanations of poor recall; it is not an Atlas-specific measured effect. (low confidence)

HNSW tuning guidance depends on intrinsic dimensionality: higher M works better on datasets with high intrinsic dimensionality and/or high recall targets. Empirical research measuring HNSW recall against exact KNN search finds that data insertion order can shift recall by up to 12 percentage points, so evaluate settings against exact nearest-neighbor results on representative data. Sources: https://github.com/nmslib/hnswlib/blob/master/ALGO_PARAMS.md ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17813

Hnswlib issue #666 reports a 3232-dimensional random-vector experiment whose 'recall' test searched every indexed vector for itself. Those figures describe self-match recovery and should not be treated as Atlas recall@k on held-out production queries. (low confidence)

Atlas documents optional hnswOptions for indexingMethod=hnsw: maxEdges ranges from 16 to 64 with default 16; numEdgeCandidates ranges from 100 to 3200 with default 100. MongoDB recommends retaining defaults unless large indexes show suboptimal recall. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Graph degree controls connectivity and graph memory. Raising Atlas maxEdges or hnswlib M can improve recall, while increasing the connections stored and the work involved in graph construction and traversal. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md ; https://github.com/nmslib/hnswlib/blob/master/ALGO_PARAMS.md

Construction breadth controls the candidate search used to choose graph connections: Atlas calls it numEdgeCandidates; hnswlib calls it ef_construction. It is separate from the number of retained connections and from query-time search breadth. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/indexes/vector-search-type.md ; https://github.com/nmslib/hnswlib/blob/master/ALGO_PARAMS.md

Increasing query breadth explores more candidates and generally trades latency for recall. Atlas numCandidates and hnswlib ef serve this role; neither should be confused with the requested result count. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/aggregation-stages/vector-search-stage.md ; https://github.com/nmslib/hnswlib/blob/master/ALGO_PARAMS.md

Evaluate approximate (ANN) results against exact nearest-neighbor (ENN) results by running the ENN query and then the ANN query and comparing the results. Pinecone's Faiss HNSW study measured recall, search time, build time and memory usage on the Sift1M dataset. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md ; https://www.pinecone.io/learn/series/faiss/hnsw/
